pk.context: 0.5 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: dull yellow, opaque, soft gelatin capsule

clues.kinetics: Absolute bioavailability is about 60%, and food lowers peak serum levels by only 10% to 15%. It is highly bound to plasma albumin (99.0%) and extensively metabolized by CYP3A4 and CYP3A5, mainly excreted in feces.
clues.substance: Molecular weight 528.5. A white to pale yellow powder with a melting point of 242° to 250°C, insoluble in water.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 0.5 mg soft gelatin capsules, dosed once daily.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated in pregnancy and in serious skin or angioedema hypersensitivity to it; impotence and decreased libido are the most common reactions.
clues.indication: Symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia in men with an enlarged prostate, to improve symptoms, reduce acute urinary retention and reduce the need for BPH-related surgery.
clues.mechanism: A competitive, specific inhibitor of both type 1 and type 2 5-alpha-reductase isoenzymes, blocking conversion of testosterone to DHT; it does not bind the androgen receptor.

tell: A terminal half-life of about five weeks sets this 5-alpha reductase inhibitor apart; levels linger for months after stopping.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: time to peak serum concentrations (T max ) of dutasteride occurs within 2 to 3 hours
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The terminal elimination half-life of dutasteride is approximately 5 weeks at steady state
